ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB\perp BD$, $ED\perp BD$, $C$ is the midpoint of line segment $BD$, and $AC\perp CE$, with $ED=1$, $BD=4$. What is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB\perp BD$ and $ED\perp BD$,\\
it follows that $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$,\\
which means $\angle A+\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
Since $AC\perp CE$,\\
we have $\angle ACE=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ECD+\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle A=\angle ECD$,\\
which implies $\triangle ABC\sim \triangle CDE$,\\
hence $\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac{BC}{DE}$\\
Given $C$ is the midpoint of segment $BD$, $ED=1$, and $BD=4$,\\
we find $BC=CD=2$,\\
therefore $\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{2}{1}$\\
leading to $AB=\boxed{4}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB\perp BD$, $ED\perp BD$, $C$ is the midpoint of line segment $BD$, and $AC\perp CE$, with $ED=1$, $BD=4$. What is the length of $AB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $AB\perp BD$ and $ED\perp BD$,\\ it follows that $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$,\\ which means $\angle A+\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\ Since $AC\perp CE$,\\ we have $\angle ACE=90^\circ$,\\ therefore $\angle ECD+\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\ thus $\angle A=\angle ECD$,\\ which implies $\triangle ABC\sim \triangle CDE$,\\ hence $\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac{BC}{DE}$\\ Given $C$ is the midpoint of segment $BD$, $ED=1$, and $BD=4$,\\ we find $BC=CD=2$,\\ therefore $\frac{AB}{2}=\frac{2}{1}$\\ leading to $AB=\boxed{4}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, BD is a horizontal base, B is at the left end, D is at the right end, and C is between B and D; AB goes vertically upward from B to A, ED goes vertically upward from D to E, there are right-angle marks at B and D in the figure, and AC and CE intersect at C and have a right-angle mark. Reasoning: From the given AB⊥BD and ED⊥BD, get ∠B=∠D=90°. C is the midpoint of BD and BD=4, so BC=CD=2. In right triangle ABC, ∠A and ∠ACB are complementary. Also AC⊥CE, and B, C, D are collinear, so ∠ACB and ∠ECD are complementary; therefore ∠A=∠ECD. Combining ∠B=∠D=90°, it can be obtained that △ABC∼△CDE. According to the corresponding sides AB↔CD and BC↔DE, AB/CD=BC/DE. Substitute CD=2, BC=2, and DE=1, obtaining AB/2=2/1, so AB=4.
